name: Encaustic
desc: Pigmented beeswax built up in fused layers you can see down through — each stroke veiled in milk by the clear wax laid over it, the whole slab never quite setting so the marks creep, while a heat gun keeps orbiting the panel and everything it passes bleeds at the edges, levels, and comes up wet.

layers.doc: how many fused wax layers are stacked — depth you can see down through

scale.doc: size of the stroke work against the frame

energy.doc: sheen off the buffed wax and the glow of the molten pass

density.doc: how much of each layer the strokes actually cover, and how crisp their edges sit

hue.doc: anchors the working palette (34 = warm wax and earths)

speed.doc: rate of the wax creep, the heat-gun pass and the light

y.doc: light elevation across the wax topography

style.doc: encaustic: hot pigmented beeswax, warm and milky with real depth · cold_wax: cold-wax medium and oil, matte, scraped, earthy · resin: clear poured resin with pigment suspended in it — glassy, deep, high gloss · relief: non-representational — the wax topography alone under a raking survey light, no pigment at all · nocturne: a dark-key near-monochrome slab, cold and melancholy

act.doc: fuse: the gun keeps passing and the wax keeps reflowing · build: layers accrete and recede across sections — the painting being made · scrape: the upper layers get cut back to reveal what is buried, then rebuilt

seed.doc: a new panel — fresh strokes, palette picks and layer order
